title: Final distance for part (1)
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for the distance when the trigger is activated in the isothermal process must be 0.4 m (or equivalent).

title: Final temperature for part (2)
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for the ambient temperature when the trigger is activated in the isochoric process must be 450 K (or equivalent in °C, e.g., 177°C).

title: Apply Boyle's Law
description: Important: For part (1), the student must correctly apply Boyle's Law (pV = constant) for the isothermal compression of the ideal gas.

title: Apply Charles's/Gay-Lussac's Law
description: Important: For part (2), the student must correctly apply the pressure-temperature law (p/T = constant at constant volume) for the isochoric heating of the ideal gas.

title: Correct initial conditions
description: Important: The student must correctly identify and use the initial pressure (p0), initial length/volume (L0), and initial temperature (T0 in Kelvin) in their calculations.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student demonstrates consistent unit handling, e.g., converting length to meters and temperature to Kelvin where necessary.

title: Misapplied gas law
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the wrong gas law (e.g., using Charles's Law for part (1) or Boyle's Law for part (2)).

title: Temperature unit error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student fails to convert the initial temperature from Celsius to Kelvin for the calculation in part (2).
